text:
maria (PM): Heads-up — Big retail customer (Acct: Fenix) asked to accelerate rollout for dedicated pinning of v2. They want a 50% traffic pin for 48h ahead of GA. Requested SLA bump. Need a quick convo on scope tradeoffs, safety gates, and experiment design.
ben (eng): We can do a phased pin but 50% immediate is risky for latency/cost. What's their acceptance criteria?
omar (sales): They need predictable latency under 200ms p95 and <2% 5xx for checkout flows, otherwise they'll pull. They also asked for a longer pin TTL if metrics look good.
elaine (data): We should define concrete metrics and a quality check set. Suggest: p95 latency, error_rate, and quality_delta on a fingerprinted eval set (20 queries). Quality delta threshold: <= 1.5% drop in correctness.
julia (research): Agree on eval set. Also add a model-output drift check (embedding cosine < 0.92) for reranking/fulfillment prompts.
ben (eng): Operationally, propose rollout steps: 5% -> 20% -> 50% (hold 2h each with automated checks). If all good, extend to 100% or maintain pin. Pin TTL default 48h unless PM extends.
maria (PM): Can we support an opt-in pin per-tenant with automatic expiration and manual override? Sales wants manual extension UI.
ben (eng): Yes. We'll expose `pin_ttl_hours` and `manual_extend` flags in the rollout API. But manual extend must create audit log and require two approvers for >72h.
nina (legal): Two approvers for >72h sounds reasonable for compliance. Also verify data residency guardrails for private tenants.
elaine (data): Monitoring: stream these metrics to the console and a slack alert channel if thresholds breach. Suggested automated rollback triggers: error_rate > 0.03 or p95_latency increase > 40% relative to baseline or quality_delta > 1.5%.
ben (eng): Draft rollout config snippet below — ops can review:
```
rollout:
  strategy: phased
  steps: [5, 20, 50]
  hold_minutes: 120
  pin_ttl_hours: 48
  manual_extend: true
  approval_threshold_hours: 72
monitors:
  - p95_latency
  - error_rate
  - quality_delta
rollback_if:
  - error_rate: ">0.03"
  - p95_latency_increase_pct: ">40"
  - quality_delta_pct: ">1.5"
```
omar (sales): Good. Customer also wants a canary traffic split that targets only checkout endpoints (not search). Can we support route-level pinning?
julia (research): Route-level pinning is doable but we need to ensure our cache/KV semantics don't leak between variants. Edge case: short context prompts + cache warmup may bias p95. Add warmup window consideration.
ben (eng): Noted — we'll add `routes` in the rollout API and a `warmup_tokens` param (default 5000) to avoid cold-start noise.
maria (PM): Acceptance criteria for go/no-go to grant 50% pin: 1) no automated rollback for 6h at 50%, 2) quality delta <= 1.5% on eval set, 3) p95_latency within 40% of baseline, 4) legal sign-off on TTL and data residency.
elaine (data): I'll own eval runs and produce a scoreboard CSV every check window.
nina (legal): I'll confirm residency constraints tomorrow.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for rollout 1799990001 at 1799990025 — monitoring hooks enabled. :rocket:
maria (PM): Thanks all — we should sync tomorrow in 30m to finalize approvals. @omar please coordinate with customer on route scoping. :thumbsup:
omar (sales): On it. I'll confirm whether checkout-only split is acceptable and push for 48h TTL with extension ability.
ben (eng): I'll open a small RFC/PRD doc with the API schema and the guardrail checklist. ETA EOD.
maria (PM): Perfect. If anyone has edge cases to add before the RFC, drop them here.
julia (research): Edge case — if customer uses replayed requests for QA, we should dedupe tokens to avoid inflated cost estimates. Add dedupe flag.
ben (eng): Good call. Will include `dedupe_replay_requests: true` default.
maria (PM): Great. Closing this thread after RFC link is posted.
